Petitioner's counsel prays for bail by imposing any stringent conditions.
The petitioner contends that the pre-trial incarceration would cause an irreversible injustice to the petitioner and family.
4. While opposing bail, the State contends that given the criminal past, the accused is likely to indulge in crime once released on bail.

REASONING:
5. In Maulana Mohd Amir Rashadi v. State of U.P., (2012) 3 SCC 382, Hon'ble 1 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:073733 CRM-M-21046-2023 Supreme Court holds, [

entities.text: Maulana Mohd Amir Rashadi v. State of U.P., (2012) 3 SCC 382
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10 ] It is not in dispute and highlighted that the second respondent is a sitting Member of Parliament facing several criminal cases.
It is also not in dispute that most of the cases ended in acquittal for want of proper witnesses or pending trial.
As observed by the High Court, merely on the basis of criminal antecedents, the claim of the second respondent cannot be rejected.

In other words, it is the duty of the Court to find out the role of the accused in the case in which he has been charged and other circumstances such as possibility of fleeing away from the jurisdiction of the Court etc.
6.

In Paramjeet Singh v. State of Punjab, CRM-M 50243 of 2021, this court observed, While considering each bail petition of the accused with a criminal history, it throws an onerous responsibility upon the Courts to act judiciously with reasonableness because arbitrariness is the antithesis of law.

entities.text: Paramjeet Singh v. State of Punjab, CRM-M 50243 of 2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The criminal history must be of cases where the accused was convicted, including the suspended sentences and all pending First Information Reports, wherein the bail petitioner stands arraigned as an accused.

In reckoning the number of cases as criminal history, the prosecutions resulting in acquittal or discharge, or when Courts quashed the FIR; the prosecution stands withdrawn, or prosecution filed a closure report; cannot be included.

Although crime is to be despised and not the criminal, yet for a recidivist, the contours of a playing field are marshy, and graver the criminal history, slushier the puddles.
7.

It is appropriate to refer to the prosecution's case from police report filed under section 173 CrPC,
Annexure P-2, which reads as follows:

That on dated 29.10.2021, Inspector Paranjeet Singh, In- charge CIA, Fazilka along with S.1. Harbans Lal No.690/Fazilka. Sirsa (Haryana) who has connections with a Gangster Ashish resident of Roorkle,
Uttarakhand, who is currently locked up in Tihar Jail, Delhi, who has connections with smugglers from Pakistan, he use to arrange Arms and ammunitions in to the Indian Border and supply it to bad elements via Ravinder.

sentences.text: He, few days back had brought in consignments from Pakistani smugglers in the area of district Fazilke and had hidden the same there only and to pick the same up Ravinder above- mentioned is coming today towards the Fazilka area.

And if barricading is done on the Nahar-Dhippan Wali pull on Fazilka- Malaut Road, then he can be apprehended and on his marking huge quantities of arms and ammunitions can be recovered which has been brought in from Pakistan.

That the information being on point and trustworthy,
this business being conducted by the accused Ravinder and Ashish abovementioned is in direct contravention of provisions of Section 25/54/59 of the Arms Act, 2 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:073733 CRM-M-21046-2023 and on having fulfilled those conditions Inspector Paramjeet Singh wrote down a Rukka against the abovementioned accused and to have a case be registered sent the Rukka through hands of present Sipahi Vinay Kumar unter 60/Fazlike to the Police Station and on receiving the Rukka, the AST Piyara Singh number 962/Fazilka had the case be registered against the abovementioned accused for the criminal activity mentioned.

Then Inspector Paramjeet Singh along with other co-personnel did barricading on the Nahar Dhippan Wali pull as conveyed in the information of the secret informer, and were conducting checking of the vehicles, when after a while the people travelling in bus No. PB-30C-9185 which was being plied by Sagar Bus Services, Sh. Mukatsar Sahib were checked, when a person sitting therein got scared on noticing the police party, he was made to disembark from the bus and his name and address was questioned from him, who his name to be Mohan son of Ram Murti, resident of House No.24, ADC Colony, Barnala Road, Sirsa, Haryana, which was found to be in conformity to the Ruga so produced.

Then Inspector Paramjeet Singh having detained Ravinder Mohan abovementioned in surveillance of the co-personnel had the bus made to leave form the scene, and interrogated the accused Ravinder Mohan abovementioned, who during the interrogation had his disclosure statement recorded under Section of Evidence Act that Yesterday on dated 28.10.2021, shish resident of Roorkie, Uttarakhand who is currently locked up in Tihar Jail conveyed to me on mobile phone that I had brought from Pakistan 2 Pistols, 47 live round ammunition and 4 hand grenades into the territory of India, and have the same hidden around 11 kilometers from Fazilka, the location of which being near the pillar on the road which displays on one side Fazilka to be 11 kilometers away and on the other side Malaut to be 38 kilometers away in the vicinity of the eucalyptus tree,
near which there is black coloured polythene bag wherein all of this has been buried.

And for this,
your work fees will be 50 thousand rupoes which is present in it.
The place where Ashish had kept his contrabands in the manner of the Pistols, cartridges, hand grenades and the Indian currency is buried can be marked out me by going along with you.
On this, the confessional statement of the accused Ravinder Mohan above mentioned was So produced.
The copy of the confessional tatement had been signed over by the accused Ravinder Mohan abovementioned in English and the witnesses had reproduced their signatures there as well.

Then, witnesses, the in presence of the accused Ravinder Mohan vs State Of Punjab on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31136464/

sentences.text: Ravinder Mohan abovementioned in tune to the disclosure statement so made by him went along with the police party pointed out the milestone at Fazilka Malaut Road, Bahad Rakba, Tahli Wala Bodla.

On one side of the milestone present on the road, it shows city Fazilka to be at 11 kilometers and on the other side city Malaut to be 38 kilometers and there is a eucalyptus tree near the milestone as well.

The search of the place informed by the accused above mentioned was done,
where in the ground near the roots of the eucalyptus tree a black coloured polythene bag was found buried there, which was taken out and checked wherein one pistol make ZIGANA- EAGLE 9x19 MM along with magazine on the backside of the hand grip of which number 111 has been written and one pistol make ZIGANA-F 9x19 MM TISAS TURKIYA along with a magazine on backside of the hand grip of which aber 7747 has been written, and 2 magazines without any marks, 47 live cartridge rounds on the butts of all of which has been ritten, and 4 plastic boxes were also founds in that very polythene bag.
All of them were opened one by one, and in each one hand grenade was found bearing mark No.86/P/01- 03/632, all coloured blue,
was recovered.

The plastic boxes were given serial numbers 1 to 4, and within the same polythene bag another polythene bag recovered, which was opened and checked and some 3 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:073733 CRM-M-21046-2023 Indian currency notes were found within, which were counted and found to be total of 25 Rs.2,000/- nots totalling to an amount of Rs. 50,000/-."
8. The petitioner's role was to transfer the consignment after digging it out.
The petitioner was aware of the contents as the same had been told to him.
He would know the disastrous consequences if such weapons and ammunition landed at the source.
Despite that, instead of informing the police, he was willing to take the shipment and proceeded the same.
As per the custody certificate dated 2-5-2023, the petitioner has been in custody since 2-11-2021.
His custody is one year, six months, and one day, which cannot be prolonged given the allegations and penal provisions invoked.

A perusal of the bail petition and the documents attached, primafacie points towards the petitioner's involvement and does not make out a case for bail and he is neither entitled to bail on merits nor on the grounds of prolonged pre-trial incarceration.
Any further discussions are likely to prejudice the petitioner; this court refrains from doing so.
9. Any observation made hereinabove is neither an expression of opinion on the merits of the case nor shall the trial Court advert to these comments.
The petition is dismissed.

However, considering the petitioners' custody, this court requests the concerned trial court to make all endeavours to conclude the trial by Sep 30, 2023, of which the prosecution evidence be completed by Aug 31, 2023, and the remaining time to provide an opportunity to the accused to lead defence evidence, if so desired.
It is clarified that this order speeding-up the trial is subject to the condition that neither the petitioner shall seek any adjournment nor try to use any tactics to delay the trial.

If they do so, this order of expediting the trial shall stand automatically recalled by resorting to Section 362, read with Section 482 Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, without any further reference to this court.

All pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.
